title: sammii-cli
description: A terminal portfolio using Ink and React to present a keyboard menu, project descriptions and contact links.
status: Packaged CLI; source reviewed at 3f7ab9e. Terminal-size and current content polish remain open.

blocks.heading: Use a different rendering surface
blocks.body: The package entry calls Ink with a React application. The interface is still built from state and components, but its target is a terminal. A gradient lettered header establishes identity, followed by a menu for About, Projects, Links and Exit.

blocks.heading: Keep navigation small
blocks.body: ink-select-input owns menu selection. Choosing an item changes a view state; Escape returns from a detail view and q can quit from the menu. Products and experiments render as colour-coded project cards. Links are displayed as terminal text. The reviewed application does not programmatically launch the selected project URL.

blocks.heading: Ship the entry as ordinary JavaScript
blocks.context: A terminal portfolio should have a small, inspectable installation path.

options.label: Require a separate compilation step for each use
options.detail: A consumer would need to build the presentation before running it.

options.label: Point the package binary at a ready JavaScript entry
options.detail: bin/cli.js has a Node shebang and imports the application directly. React.createElement keeps JSX compilation out of this package’s runtime path.

blocks.outcome: The source is an npm-style command package whose entry renders the menu directly through Ink.

blocks.heading: Terminal constraints need their own review
blocks.body: The current views use fixed content widths and a fixed-size lettered header. A terminal-size matrix is needed before claiming that they adapt to narrow windows. The application uses Ink’s exit function; this review did not establish a custom cursor-reset handler, a universal hyperlink experience or startup-time measurements. The next pass should bring its project data into line with the current web portfolio and verify navigation in real terminals.
